svg.text: The five addressing shapes
The mode is a property of the mnemonic, not of an operand. Operands are listed in the order the row's signature uses.
Vector buffer
address = descriptor base + (index if M.idxen1) + (offset if M.offen1)
RK8 base selector (or the zero source) · RJ8x4 four-register descriptor · VQ8 byte offset · UO12 constant offset
M.offen1 and M.idxen1 each enable one contribution · M.bl11 is set for the buffer forms
The descriptor is four scalar registers, so its base is aligned to four. An unused index encodes the zero source.
Flat
address = the 64-bit value held in the aligned vector register pair
VJ8x2 or VK8x2 absolute address pair · RK8x2 zero scalar pair · VA8 compare or read-modify-write data
VD8 destination tuple · M.bl11 and M.bl21 are the memory behaviour controls
There is no descriptor, so nothing in the encoding bounds the access. This is the mode a host constrains least.
Texture and image
texel = image descriptor + coordinate window
RK8x8 or RK9x8 image descriptor · RA8x4 sampler descriptor · VJ8x8 coordinate window · VD8x4 result
X0_4 channel mask · M.un1 unnormalized · M.na1 array form · M.rsz1 resource width · M.bl11, M.bl21
The window is an upper bound: a variant consumes a prefix whose length depends on its coordinate tuple.
Shared memory
element = workgroup allocation base + offset
VK8, VJ8, VA8 and VD8 vector registers, positionally · X0_16 byte or element offset
PJ2 is the predicate position
No shared base is encoded: the launch supplies the segment. The address unit and lane mapping are UNRESOLVED.
Scalar memory
address = the scalar pair's value + UO20
RJ8x2 or RJ8x4 address pair or descriptor · UO20 unsigned constant offset · GK8 zero source
RD8 result tuple · PJ2 is the predicate position
The result lands in the scalar file, so a wide load is a tuple of scalar registers.
Operand classes and modifier kinds are in the operands chapter; per-mode behaviour is in the memory and image family chapter.
